# Give measured work a name

[Record real Euler updates with nested scopes, a custom scalar metric and a collective JSON export.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

A useful profiling report connects measured time with identifiable work.
This refactors the synthetic spin demonstration into four Euler updates
of $u_t=-u$ on a small vector. Each rank computes its own identical vector;
this is a profiling-contract example, not a distributed speedup experiment.

## Nest regions around actual operations

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="scopes" dedent=4}
```

`step` encloses `step/rhs` and `step/update`. Inclusive time contains child
regions; exclusive time removes their contribution. A manual scope records
the norm calculation separately. The session explicitly registers the
custom `rms` frame metric before setting it. Unknown scalar metric names
would otherwise be ignored.
The three memory counters passed to the frame helper are zero because this
example does not measure memory usage; they are not evidence of zero allocations.

Four frames mean four recorded outer iterations. The report's call count
reflects frames in which a path recorded time, not a general-purpose count
of every invocation of an arbitrarily repeated inner scope. Repeated work
within a frame contributes to its accumulated path time.
The implicit `diagnostics` parent groups the measured `norm` child; it has
no enclosing timed scope of its own. Its zero time and placeholder count
must not be interpreted as a measured outer-region invocation.

## Export and print collectively

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="export" dedent=4}
```

Every rank participates in the export and aggregate report. The JSON is
`results/profile.json`, with schema version 3, a `teaching` run identifier
and equation metadata. Each rank's frames remain separately identifiable.
The default console statistic combines per-rank totals as documented by
the profiling interface; it is not an additional elapsed wall-clock timer.

## Keep numerical and timing checks separate

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --launcher=none
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --ranks=2 --launcher=mpirun
```

The empty input is unused. The numerical oracle after $m$ updates is
$u=(1-.01)^m$. Tests check the final recurrence, all four RMS metrics on
every rank, the exported frame counts and region hierarchy, and finite
nonnegative recorded durations. No duration is promoted to a benchmark
claim. Timing instrumentation also has overhead, especially for such tiny
regions; use larger representative work when investigating performance.
See the
[profiling session contract](https://github.com/VTT-ProperTune/OpenPFC/blob/master/include/openpfc/kernel/profiling/session.hpp)
and the handbook's profiling guide for larger applications.

The complete [C++ model](model.cpp) and [starting input](input.json)
are available with this lesson.

:::
